note: The context for the law-time date probe (DMN-EXPORT-PROGRAM-MODEL-SPEC.md 15.6).
`{"$date": "YYYY-MM-DD"}` is the fixture vocabulary's ONLY way to say
"this is a FEEL date". Deliberately an explicit tag and NOT an ISO-shape
sniff on strings: both harnesses convert by declared type and never by
appearance (see the BigDecimal note on KieDmnCheck.jsonToFeel), and a sniff
would silently retype any genuine string that happened to look like a date.
The three cases pin the interval convention itself: the low end is CLOSED
and the high end is OPEN, so the day of a change belongs to the new regime
and the day before belongs to the old one. Case C reaches the floor row.

cases.name: A. the day of the 2024 change -- low end is CLOSED
B. the day before -- high end is OPEN
C. before commencement -- the floor row fires
